wisdom.definition: An element of personal character that enables one to distinguish the wise from the unwise.

wise.definition: Showing good judgement or the benefit of experience.

wish.definition: A desire, hope, or longing for something or for something to happen.

wishes.definition: A desire, hope, or longing for something or for something to happen.

with.definition: A flexible, slender shoot or twig, especially when used as a band or for binding; a withy.

within.definition: In or into the interior; inside.

wonder.definition: A sense of awe, astonishment and curiosity, inspired by unexpected events, novel experiences and inexplicable circumstances, sometimes accompanied by surprise, shock or reverence.

wonderful.definition: Tending to excite wonder; surprising, extraordinary.

word.definition: Having a value of; proper to be exchanged for.

words.definition: Having a value of; proper to be exchanged for.

wore.definition: An adjustable dam placed across a river to regulate the flow of water downstream.

world.definition: The subjective human experience, regarded collectively; human collective existence; existence in general; the reality we live in.

worlds.definition: The subjective human experience, regarded collectively; human collective existence; existence in general; the reality we live in.

worth.definition: Having a value of; proper to be exchanged for.

would.definition: Past tense of will; usually followed by a bare infinitive.

wrings.definition: Often followed by out: to squeeze or twist (something moist) tightly so that liquid is forced out.

writers.definition: A person who writes, or produces literary work; an author can refer to themselves as "the writer".

writing.definition: To form letters, words or symbols on a surface in order to communicate.

writings.definition: To form letters, words or symbols on a surface in order to communicate.

wrongly.definition: In violation of a moral or other standard, code, or convention; in an unfair, unjust, dishonest, or immoral manner; wrongly convicted is synonymous with wrongful conviction and miscarriage of justice.

wrung.definition: Often followed by out: to squeeze or twist (something moist) tightly so that liquid is forced out.

xi.definition: The 14th letter of Classical and Modern Greek. The 15th in Ancient and Old Greek.

years.definition: In, on, or at this place (a place perceived to be close to the speaker); compare there.

yes.definition: An affirmative expression; an answer that shows agreement or acceptance.

yesterday.definition: The day immediately before today; one day ago.

yet.definition: Thus far; up to the present; up to some unspecified time.

yield.definition: To give as a result or outcome; to produce or render.

york.definition: To bowl a yorker at a batsman, especially to get a batsman out in this way.

you.definition: To address (a person) using the pronoun you (in the past, especially to use you rather than thou, when you was considered more formal).
